notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (data.js fy 'Dec 2025'). The source is Samsung Electronics' English '2025 Business Report' (K-IFRS, file name 2025_4Q_Interim_Report.pdf), hosted on Samsung's own CDN (images.samsung.com) and linked from samsung.com/global/ir. Figures in millions of KRW converted to billions. RELATION: 'founding-family' is used. The report lists Lee Jae-yong as a 'Related party of the major shareholder' (Samsung Life Insurance), as is Ra-hee Hong. OWNERSHIP BASIS: all percentages are as stated in the report and are percentages of common (voting) shares issued, including treasury shares; preferred stakes are percentages of the preferred class. Nothing is recomputed. Lee's common holding was unchanged at 97,414,196 shares, and his stake rose from 1.63% to 1.65% only because Samsung cancelled 50,144,628 treasury common shares in 2025. He also holds 137,757 preferred shares (0.02% of preferred), not included. The report gives no percentage of all shares (common plus preferred), and pctVoting is left null because the report gives a stake of common shares, not voting power. Lee's main economic exposure is indirect, as Samsung C&T's major shareholder (19.93%, 21.00% after Ra-hee Hong's January 2, 2026 gift), and that is not added. FAMILY: the 19.84% related-party total already includes Lee's own 1.65% along with Samsung Life Insurance (8.51% + 0.07% special accounts), Samsung C&T (5.05%), Samsung Fire & Marine (1.49%), Samsung foundations, Ra-hee Hong (1.49%), Boo-jin Lee (0.71%), Seo-hyun Lee (0.77%) and affiliate executives. Samsung Life and Samsung C&T, though over 5% each, are therefore not listed as separate holders. BLACKROCK: very stale. Samsung bases it on a February 7, 2019 mass-holding report (holdings as of January 28, 2019). DIVIDENDS: the consolidated cash-flow 'Dividends paid' of KRW 9,897,183m includes dividends paid by subsidiaries to non-controlling interests. The parent company's separate cash-flow line (KRW 9,809,646m) is used as the cash paid to Samsung Electronics' own shareholders; it covers common and preferred shareholders together. BUYBACKS: 'Purchase of treasury shares' is the same KRW 8,189,263m in the consolidated and separate statements (118,314,495 common and 16,465,497 preferred shares bought in 2025). Unlike Richemont's employee-plan hedging, these purchases are counted gross: the two 2025 programmes (KRW 3,039,395m resolved February 18, 2025 and KRW 3,911,908m resolved July 8, 2025) were stated to be 'to enhance shareholder value and facilitate stock-based compensation for executives and employees', the rest settled the November 2024 programme whose shares were cancelled in February 2025, and the report's plan for January–June 2026 is to cancel 73,359,314 of the common shares acquired. In 2025, 50,144,628 common and 6,912,036 preferred shares were cancelled and 6,040,880 common shares (KRW 345,637m at cost) were granted to employees; the report gives no purchase amount for the employee-designated part alone. STOCK COMP: new in FY2025. The consolidated equity statement credits KRW 711,447m of 'Share-based payment' to other components of equity; Note 20 describes 30 shares granted to every employee (KRW 199,092m), retention grants to high performers (KRW 182,544m), executive restricted stock and long-term incentives settled in shares, and a performance stock unit plan (KRW 166,614m expensed). GEOGRAPHY: Samsung's five regions as reported to its Management Committee.
